outputs.L1: The present invention relates to a disposable diaper for absorbing and containing excreted urine and feces. The disposable diaper is divided into a front surface part configured to contact the wearer’s abdomen, a rear surface part configured to contact the wearer’s back, and a gap part extending longitudinally between the front and rear surface parts so as to pass between the wearer’s legs. The disposable diaper includes: a base layer provided with an absorber at an upper end thereof in the lengthwise direction relative to the center of the gap part, and first elastic members disposed on both longitudinal sides so as to surround the wearer’s legs; a cover layer positioned over the absorber so as to cover the absorber; and a skin-contact layer positioned over the base layer so as to cover the cover layer. The skin-contact layer includes an inlet cutting part cut to a predetermined length to allow urine and feces to readily reach the cover layer or the absorber, and second elastic members disposed longitudinally on both sides of the inlet cutting part, spaced apart therefrom at predetermined intervals, and configured to come into close contact with the skin of the lower portion of the wearer’s buttocks.
outputs.L2:
The invention concerns a disposable diaper designed to collect and absorb urine and feces. The diaper is divided into a front portion that contacts the wearer’s abdomen, a rear portion that contacts the wearer’s back, and a crotch portion extending longitudinally between the front and rear portions and passing between the wearer’s legs. The diaper comprises:

- a base layer having an absorbent body located above the longitudinal center of the crotch portion and first elastic members arranged longitudinally along both sides to surround the wearer’s legs;
- a cover layer disposed over and covering the absorbent body; and
- a skin-contact layer positioned over the base layer and covering the cover layer, the skin-contact layer including an inlet slit formed to a specified length to facilitate the passage of urine and feces to the cover layer or absorbent body, as well as second elastic members extending longitudinally on both sides, spaced from the inlet slit by predetermined distances, and configured to fit closely against the skin along the lower part of the wearer’s buttocks.
outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a disposable diaper configured to absorb and contain bodily waste, including urine and feces. The diaper includes a front section positioned against the wearer’s abdomen and a rear section positioned against the wearer’s back. These sections are connected by an intermediate gap section that extends between the wearer’s legs when the diaper is in use.

The diaper further includes a base layer containing an absorbent body for retaining bodily fluids. First elastic members are arranged along both longitudinal sides of the base layer to provide a close fit around the wearer’s legs and help prevent leakage. A cover layer is positioned above the absorbent body and cooperates with the base layer to enclose and retain the absorbent body.

A skin-contact layer is disposed over the cover layer and is configured to contact the wearer’s skin. This layer includes an inlet opening through which urine and feces can pass into the interior of the diaper. The skin-contact layer also includes spaced second elastic members arranged to fit closely against the wearer’s buttocks. Together, these components improve fit, guide waste into the diaper, and help contain it securely.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a disposable diaper designed to improve the containment and absorption of urine and feces while providing a secure and comfortable fit. The diaper includes a front waist section, a rear waist section, and a crotch section extending between the front and rear sections. Together, these sections form a garment-like structure that can be fitted around the wearer’s waist, hips, buttocks, and legs.

The diaper comprises an absorbent base layer capable of receiving and retaining bodily waste, a cover layer disposed on the outer side of the absorbent base layer, and a skin-contact layer positioned on the wearer-facing side. The cover layer may serve as a liquid-resistant backing that helps prevent absorbed liquid from passing through to clothing or bedding. The skin-contact layer is arranged to remain close to the wearer’s body and includes a cut or opening that functions as an inlet through which urine and feces can pass toward the absorbent base layer.

Elastic members are provided along regions corresponding to the wearer’s legs and buttocks. When the diaper is worn, these elastic members contract to hold the skin-contact layer gently against the body and to maintain the inlet in an appropriate position. The leg elastic members form resilient seals around the thighs, while the buttock elastic members improve conformity to the contours of the rear body. This arrangement reduces gaps that might otherwise permit bodily waste to escape.

The inlet in the skin-contact layer enables discharged urine and feces to move away from the skin and into the interior waste-receiving region of the diaper. Urine is directed toward and absorbed by the absorbent base layer, whereas feces can be received and retained below the skin-contact layer. By separating the wearer’s skin from collected waste, the diaper can reduce spreading, improve cleanliness, and limit prolonged contact between the skin and bodily discharges.

The coordinated action of the inlet, the absorbent base layer, and the elastic members helps keep the diaper properly positioned during movement. Close contact around the legs and buttocks improves overall fit and creates barriers against leakage without substantially interfering with comfort. As a result, the invention provides a disposable diaper having improved waste guidance, containment, absorption, and leak prevention, while also enhancing wearer comfort and hygiene.
outputs.L5:
**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it plays an essential role in communication. It points to something specific: not just a book, but *the* book; not simply a moment, but *the* moment. With only three letters, it creates clarity, emphasis, and shared understanding. Often unnoticed, “the” quietly connects ideas and gives meaning to countless sentences.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe the construction of a disposable diaper in the style of an international patent application, emphasizing the lengthwise arrangement of its layers, absorbent element, inlet cutting part, and spaced elastic members.
counterfactuals.output:
**Disposable Diaper**

A disposable diaper (1) has a longitudinal direction (L) extending between a front waist region (2) and a rear waist region (3), and a transverse direction (W) orthogonal thereto. The diaper (1) comprises, in a thickness direction, a liquid-permeable topsheet (10), a liquid-impermeable backsheet (20), and an absorbent element (30) disposed between the topsheet (10) and the backsheet (20).

The absorbent element (30) is elongated in the longitudinal direction (L) and includes an absorbent core (31), optionally enclosed by a core-wrapping sheet (32). The absorbent core (31) extends through at least a crotch region (4) located between the front and rear waist regions (2, 3), and may comprise pulp fibers, superabsorbent polymer particles, or a combination thereof. An acquisition or diffusion layer (33) may be arranged between the topsheet (10) and the absorbent core (31) and may extend lengthwise over at least a central portion of the absorbent element (30).

An inlet cutting part (40) is formed in at least one layer positioned on a wearer-facing side of the absorbent core (31). The inlet cutting part (40) is elongated in the longitudinal direction (L) and defines an inlet through which bodily exudates are introduced toward the absorbent element (30). The inlet cutting part (40) may comprise a slit, aperture, notch, or removed portion of the topsheet (10), the acquisition layer (33), or an auxiliary sheet arranged therebetween. Preferably, the inlet cutting part (40) is located in the crotch region (4) and is aligned with a longitudinal centerline (C) of the diaper (1). Opposed longitudinal edges of the inlet cutting part (40) may remain separable or may be urged apart during use.

A plurality of elastic members (50) is disposed at mutually spaced positions in the transverse direction (W) on opposite sides of the inlet cutting part (40). Each elastic member (50) extends lengthwise along at least part of the crotch region (4) and is secured under tension to the topsheet (10), an intermediate sheet, or a pair of barrier cuff sheets (60). The elastic members (50) are separated from respective longitudinal edges of the inlet cutting part (40), thereby defining non-elastic or reduced-tension spacing regions (51) between the inlet cutting part (40) and the elastic members (50). Upon contraction, the spaced elastic members (50) raise or shape the wearer-facing layers around the inlet cutting part (40), while maintaining the inlet in fluid communication with the absorbent element (30).

The backsheet (20) may include a breathable liquid-impermeable film and an outer nonwoven layer (21). Leg elastic members (70) may additionally extend along opposite longitudinal side margins of the diaper (1), outward of the absorbent element (30), and waist elastic members (71) may extend in the transverse direction (W) in one or both waist regions (2, 3).

Accordingly, when viewed in the thickness direction, the diaper (1) comprises a lengthwise-arranged laminate in which the inlet cutting part (40), the absorbent element (30), and the spaced elastic members (50) extend generally parallel to the longitudinal direction (L), the elastic members (50) being positioned laterally outward of and spaced from the inlet cutting part (40). This arrangement facilitates entry and lengthwise distribution of bodily exudates while reducing leakage toward the side margins.
